prompt:
A vertical aerial photograph taken for a lake authority's boat wash survey, the frame filed each summer.

The lake is deep and open here and the water is otherwise flat. Two boats are running straight and steady across the frame at the same moment, both well clear of the shore: a heavy displacement launch and a light planing boat. Each drags its own wake behind it, the two arms of foam opening out from the boat and the run of curved crests inside them, and both wakes are complete and clear in the frame. Beside each boat the survey has printed that boat's speed through the water in knots on a small tag: 6 beside the launch and 20 beside the planing boat. A scale bar sits in one corner of the frame.

The authority argues about wash from these frames, so each wake has to open out the way a wake from a boat at that speed on deep water really opens out, and the crests inside each wake have to be spaced the way that boat's speed really spaces them. How wide each wake opens and how the crests fall is what the survey is for -- I am deliberately not telling you either. No angle figure, no wavelength figure and no note goes into the frame: apart from the two speed tags and the scale bar there is no text in the picture. Both boats, both complete wakes and both tags are in the frame together.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show water from above with two boats on it, each leaving a spreading trail of foam behind it? An aerial photograph, a survey frame or an overhead view all count as yes. Answer no only if the image instead shows a bare card stating an answer with none of that around it, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

steps.target: a boat running across the water with a trail of foam behind it

steps.read_crop: Copy the speed figure printed on the tag beside this boat. Write digits only.
Is the wedge of foam behind this boat opened out wider than the wedge behind the other boat, about the same, or narrower? Answer with one word: wider, same, or narrower.
